statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 80%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ futures trade at 29,457.00, up 0.03%, inside an overnight band of 29,364.00 to 29,480.25 that has not widened in the past hour and spans only about 0.40%. Both extremes of that band have been rejected, which is retracement behaviour rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions, and VIX flat at 16.46 confirms no tail repricing in options. Stress stays extreme because Brent near $101, a 10-year at 4.84% and an active tanker conflict in the Gulf make the environment difficult even where mean reversion is intact, with back-to-back producer and consumer price releases still ahead. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open.
headline: NQ futures hold 29,457.00, up 0.03%, inside an unchanged 0.40% overnight band with VIX flat at 16.46, while Brent near $101 and a 4.84% 10-year keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC PPI release
body: Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,457.00, up 8.25 points or 0.03%, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,480.25. That band spans roughly 0.40% and has not widened over the past hour; price sits in its upper third having earlier rejected the low, so both extremes have now been faded. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range. Asian equities were broadly weaker, with the MSCI Asia Pacific index down 0.8%, the Hang Seng down 1.4% and the ASX 200 down 1.5%, yet that weakness has again failed to transmit into directional NQ structure. Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive but are no longer uniformly tightening. Brent trades at $100.90, easing 0.31%, and WTI at $96.02 after US and Iranian forces exchanged strikes on shipping and Strait of Hormuz transits collapsed to roughly ten commodity ships a day. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.837%, up 3.1 basis points and its highest since 2023, while the 2-year eased 1.2 basis points to 4.43%; that split points to term premium rather than a hawkish front-end repricing. VIX at 16.46 is unchanged and remains the clearest counterweight: implied volatility is not pricing a discontinuity. Latest-session breadth is internally conflicted, with megacaps 1 of 8 higher on 2.59% dispersion as Meta rose 6.55% on an AI agent launch while Alphabet fell 2.28%, against semiconductors 5 of 7 higher. Conflicting breadth of that kind lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The scheduled path is dense: August producer prices and weekly jobless claims arrive at 12:30 UTC today, consensus +0.4% headline and +0.3% core against a 0% prior, followed by August consumer prices at 12:30 UTC on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, where futures imply roughly 62% odds of a rate increase. Consistent with the standing method, an unreleased number raises Stress and uncertainty rather than observed Tail; only the price path after a release can establish tail conditions. Tail is therefore held at 10% and Stress at 80%. Confidence is 88% on live futures, index, yield, oil and volatility readings alongside a calendar corroborated across independent sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 05:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 7% to 20% and has settled into an 8-11% band overnight as retracements kept appearing. Stress climbed from 75% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set fresh 2023 highs. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail in a 10-14% range through the Asian and European sessions, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-PPI repricing overlaps the US cash open, then returns it to 11-13% overnight into the CPI session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout because oil above $100, a 2023-high 10-year and an active Gulf conflict are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 79% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.
